qa.q: How long is the contract and what is the notice period?
qa.answer: The contract runs for **12 months** from 1 January 2025, with **automatic renewal** [1]. To end it, a registered letter must be sent at least **30 days before expiry** [1]. Amendment no. 2 does not change this term, it only adds a price review clause [2].

sources.passage: This contract is entered into for a term of twelve (12) months from 1 January 2025. It renews automatically unless terminated by either party by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt sent at least thirty (30) days before its expiry.
sources.highlight: at least thirty (30) days before its expiry

sources.passage: All other provisions of the contract, in particular its term and termination terms, remain unchanged. Prices may be reviewed once a year, up to 3%.
sources.highlight: in particular its term and termination terms, remain unchanged

qa.q: What are the penalties for late delivery?
qa.answer: For late delivery, the supplier owes **1% of the order amount per week of delay** [1], capped at **10%** of the total [1]. Beyond four weeks, you may cancel the order at no cost [1].

sources.passage: Any late delivery attributable to the supplier shall give rise to penalties equal to 1% of the order amount excluding tax per week of delay, up to 10% of that amount. Beyond four (4) weeks of delay, the client may cancel the order concerned without compensation.
sources.highlight: 1% of the order amount excluding tax per week of delay

qa.q: Does the March invoice match the contract price?
qa.answer: Almost. The March invoice uses a unit price of **€52.50** [1], whereas the contract sets **€50.00** [2]. Amendment no. 2 allows a review of at most **3%** per year [3], i.e. €51.50 maximum: the **€1.00 per unit** gap is worth raising with the supplier.

sources.passage: Ref. PRD-118 — Cartridges pack of 10 — Qty 40 — Unit price excl. tax €52.50 — Total excl. tax €2,100.00
2025 price list: Ref. PRD-118, cartridges pack of 10, unit price excluding tax: €50.00.
Prices may be reviewed once a year, on the contract anniversary date, up to 3% of the price in force.
sources.highlight: up to 3% of the price in force

qa.q: What was decided at the last supplier meeting?
qa.answer: At the 14 March meeting, three decisions were made [1]: the supplier **will issue a credit note** for the March price gap, deliveries will move to **every two weeks**, and a follow-up is set for **30 April** [1].

sources.passage: Decisions: 1) the supplier issues a credit note for the price gap found on the March invoice; 2) fortnightly deliveries from April; 3) next follow-up on 30 April.
sources.highlight: the supplier issues a credit note

qa.q: How many remote work days are allowed?
qa.answer: Each employee may work remotely up to **2 days a week** [1], once the probation period is over [1]. Days are agreed with the manager and **Tuesday remains a shared office day** for the whole team [1].

sources.passage: After the probation period, every employee may work remotely two (2) days per week, agreed with their manager. Tuesday is a mandatory office day for all teams.

qa.q: How do I request leave, and how far in advance?
qa.answer: Leave is requested in the HR tool, **at least 4 weeks ahead** for more than 5 days off, and **one week** otherwise [1]. The manager replies within **5 working days** [1]. In summer, at least **2 consecutive weeks** must be taken between May and October [1].

sources.passage: Leave requests are made in the HR tool at least four weeks in advance for an absence of more than five days, and one week in advance otherwise. The manager replies within five working days. A leave of at least two consecutive weeks is taken between 1 May and 31 October.
sources.highlight: at least four weeks in advance

qa.q: What was said about meal vouchers at the last works council?
qa.answer: According to the works council recording, management announced a **face value increase to €11** from June, with **60% paid by the employer** [1]. A digital card will replace paper vouchers by the end of the year [1].

sources.passage: [12:40] Management: "For meal vouchers, the face value goes up to eleven euros from June, still sixty percent paid by the company. And we move everyone to the digital card by December."
sources.highlight: the face value goes up to eleven euros from June

qa.q: How does the health plan cover glasses?
qa.answer: The health plan covers glasses up to **€350 every two years** (frames + lenses), including **€100 maximum for frames** [1]. Contact lenses are covered up to **€150 per year** [1].

sources.passage: Optical equipment (frames + 2 lenses): €350 per two-year period, including €100 maximum for frames. Prescribed contact lenses: €150 per calendar year.

qa.answer: Go-live is planned for **15 September 2025** [1]. It was **pushed back two weeks** at the February steering committee, to leave time to finish load testing [2].

privacy.title: Cookies and personal data
privacy.subtitle: Your data is isolated per workspace and never sold. Here's simply what's stored, and why.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: This site uses no advertising cookies and no third-party targeting cookies. Two audience measurement tools are used. The first, SEO Monitor, is exempt from consent and described in the Audience measurement section below. The second records page views, time spent and an approximate country derived from your IP address, but only if you accept it in the banner shown on your first visit: it relies on a temporary session id that is cleared when you close the tab, and never tracks app pages (spaces, share links, dashboard). Your choice is kept in your browser's local storage and you can change it by clearing this site's data.

sections.title: Local storage (localStorage)
sections.body: Your session (once logged in) and any share links you use are saved in your browser's local storage (localStorage), solely to avoid logging in again on every page. They are never sent to a third party. You can clear them at any time by clearing this site's data in your browser.

sections.title: Account and workspace data
sections.body: Your email address and your password (hashed) are required to create an account. The documents you upload, their indexed content and your conversations are stored on the server hosting the service (dedicated database and vector store), partitioned per workspace, and are never resold nor used to train an AI model. To generate an answer, read an image or index a document, the relevant text is sent to our AI inference provider, Mistral AI, a French company whose processing takes place within the European Union (see the Technical providers section below). Audio file transcription, on the other hand, runs on our own servers and is never sent to any third party.

sections.title: What you upload
sections.body: You remain responsible for the documents you upload and for the information you type into conversations. Before importing a file, make sure you are entitled to do so: do not upload documents belonging to a third party without their permission, and avoid particularly sensitive data (health data, identity documents, bank details, passwords) where it is not essential to your use. The content of your documents is processed automatically to answer your questions, and a share link grants access to an entire workspace: check what it contains before sending it, and revoke the link as soon as it is no longer needed. You can delete a document, a workspace or your entire account at any time.

sections.title: Contact form
sections.body: If you use the contact form, your name, email and message are kept so we can reply to you. This information is never resold or shared with third parties, and is never used for marketing outreach.

sections.title: Technical providers
sections.body: To operate, the service relies on a small number of providers acting as processors and bound by contract: a host (OVHcloud, servers located in France), an AI inference provider (Mistral AI, a French company, processing carried out within the European Union), an email delivery service (address verification, password reset, newsletter) and an analytics tool (only if you accept it). Each receives only the data strictly necessary for its service and is not allowed to use it for other purposes, for advertising, or to train its own models. Your documents, conversations and the associated vector index are hosted and processed exclusively within the European Union. The email provider, however, may be established outside the European Union: it receives no content from your documents, and the corresponding transfers are governed by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses. The current, named list of these processors is available on request via the contact form.

sections.title: Data controller and retention periods
sections.body: The data controller is the publisher of the service, whose full identity appears on the Legal notice page; they can be reached through the contact form. Your account data, documents and conversations are kept for as long as your account exists, then deleted as soon as you delete your account. Messages sent through the contact form are kept for the time needed to handle your request. A newsletter subscription is kept until you unsubscribe.

sections.title: Your rights (GDPR)
sections.body: Export your data: from My Account, download a file with all of your data in one click. Delete your account: from My Account (danger zone), immediate and permanent deletion of your account and workspaces. Newsletter: every email includes a one-click unsubscribe link, no login required. For any other request (rectification, objection), use the contact form.

privacy.footnote: This page describes the service as operated on this website. Since the software can also be self-hosted, an instance installed and administered by another organisation is that organisation's responsibility.

audience.title: Audience measurement
paragraphs: This site uses SEO Monitor, a self-hosted audience measurement tool, to produce anonymous traffic statistics (pages viewed, where visits come from, time spent, device type). This data is used solely to keep the site running properly and to improve it.

A random identifier is kept in your browser for up to 13 months. Your IP address is never stored: it is only used, transiently, to derive an approximate country and city. The data is neither combined with other processing nor shared with third parties, and is kept for up to 25 months.

Purpose and legal basis: audience measurement of the site, based on the publisher's legitimate interest in knowing how the site is used (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). This processing is exempt from consent under Article 82 of the French Data Protection Act and the CNIL guidelines on trackers.
Data collected: pages viewed, visit source, time spent, scroll depth, device type, browser, language, approximate country and city. The IP address is not stored.
Tracker and retention periods: sm_vid identifier, saved in the browser's local storage for audience measurement, for up to 13 months (exempt from consent). Statistics are kept for up to 25 months.
Recipients: no third parties. The data is hosted on an OVH server located in France.

Your rights: you have the right to access, rectify, erase, object to and restrict the processing, which you can exercise through the contact form. You may also lodge a complaint with the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).

items.question: What is {{brand}}?
items.answer: {{brand}} connects your business documents (PDF, images, web pages, DOCX, TXT, Markdown) to an AI with sourced answers, in spaces siloed per client or file. Built for firms, agencies and teams managing multiple clients.

items.question: Do I need an account to use it?
items.answer: Yes, an account is required to use {{brand}}, including to open a share link. That's what lets each space know exactly who accessed it and with which role.

items.question: What is a workspace?
items.answer: A workspace groups documents and conversations around a given topic. Each workspace is isolated: nothing is shared between two different spaces. Several people can collaborate on the same workspace.

items.question: What roles exist on a workspace?
items.answer: Owner (creates the space, manages members and share links, can delete it), editor (can chat with the assistant and add documents), and viewer (can only browse history and documents, without writing).

items.question: How do share links work?
items.answer: From a space you own, generate a link with the viewer or editor role. Anyone signed in who opens that link gets access to the space with that role - if they don't have an account yet, they're prompted to create one first. You can revoke a link at any time.

items.question: Which document formats are supported?
items.answer: PDF (native text or scanned, with automatic OCR by a vision AI), images (JPG, PNG, WEBP...), web pages, DOCX, TXT and Markdown. Documents are automatically chunked and indexed for search.

items.question: Can the AI search the web?
items.answer: Yes. When a question needs current information (news, weather, prices...), the assistant automatically detects the need and completes its answer via a self-hosted search engine, with no API key and no tracking.

items.question: Does my data stay private?
items.answer: Yes, within the European Union. Your documents, embeddings and conversations are stored on our servers in France, at OVHcloud. To generate an answer, the relevant text is sent to Mistral AI, a French publisher whose processing takes place in the EU - nothing goes to a provider outside the European Union, and your data is never used to train a model. Audio transcription does not even leave our servers.

items.question: How do I enable two-factor verification (2FA)?
items.answer: From the Account page, Security section, click Enable next to "Two-factor verification". Scan the code with your authenticator app, then confirm with the 6-digit code.

items.question: What happens if I delete a document or conversation by mistake?
items.answer: Every workspace gets an automatic backup (at most once a day, kept on a 7-day rolling window). An instance administrator can restore the space to an earlier state from the admin dashboard.

items.question: Are there usage limits?
items.answer: Yes, to prevent abuse, each account has usage limits: 3 workspaces, 5 members per workspace, 500 MB of storage per workspace and 50 AI questions per day. The question counter resets every day.
